name: FormControl
description: A context-providing wrapper that connects a label, input, helper text, and error message via ARIA. Exposes a React context so child components (FormLabel, FormHelperText, FormErrorMessage, Input, Textarea, etc.) can co-ordinate their IDs, required state, disabled state, and invalid state without prop-drilling.

notes: FormControl generates a stable id via useId when none is provided; all child components derive their own ids from this root id.
FormLabel renders a <label> with htmlFor pointing to the root id, creating a native accessible name relationship.
FormHelperText renders with id='{id}-helper'; inputs should include this in aria-describedby.
FormErrorMessage renders with id='{id}-error' and role='alert'; only mounts when invalid is true so the alert fires at the right moment.
aria-required is reflected by the Input when required=true is set on the FormControl.
aria-invalid is reflected by the Input when invalid=true is set on the FormControl.
aria-disabled is reflected by the Input when disabled=true is set on the FormControl.

id.description: The root id shared across all child components. Auto-generated if omitted.

required.description: Marks the field as required. Propagated to label and input via context.

disabled.description: Disables the field. Propagated to all child components via context.

invalid.description: Marks the field as invalid. Shows the error message and applies danger border to the input.

children.description: Should contain FormLabel, an input-type component, and optionally FormHelperText or FormErrorMessage.

className.description: Additional CSS class names to apply to the wrapper div.

children.description: Error message content. Only rendered when context.invalid is true.

do: Always place FormLabel as a direct or nested child of FormControl so it picks up the correct id.
Use FormHelperText for persistent guidance and FormErrorMessage for validation feedback — not both with overlapping content.
Supply a meaningful id prop when server-rendering to avoid hydration mismatches from auto-generated ids.
Keep FormErrorMessage content concise and actionable.
dont: Do not use FormLabel outside a FormControl — it will have no htmlFor target.
Do not render FormErrorMessage when the form has not yet been submitted or touched, to avoid prematurely alarming users.
Do not nest FormControl instances — context will be overwritten by the innermost provider.
